title: Deeds first (Avot 3:9)
hookLine: Chanina ben Dosa: when deeds exceed wisdom, the wisdom endures
tomorrow: can being liked by people mean anything to God?

cards: Sawdust in your hair, wet paint on your sneakers, a drill whining somewhere backstage. Set-building day smells like pine and turpentine, and nobody's reading anything. So what happens if you do more than you know?
Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa says the wisdom lasts. Whoever's deeds are more than his wisdom, his wisdom endures, he says in Avot. Whoever's wisdom is more than his deeds, his wisdom won't endure.

teach.b: Feel the order in that. Wisdom that stays in the head is like a recipe never cooked: it fades. Wisdom that's already in the hands has somewhere to live.
Chanina ben Dosa adds a twin saying just before it: whoever's fear of sin comes before his wisdom, his wisdom endures. Character first, then knowledge.
Second, the tradition remembers a moment when a whole people put doing first. At Sinai, before the details, they answer Moses: "All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient."

teach.h: WE WILL DO, AND WE WILL HEAR.
teach.b: In Hebrew, na'aseh v'nishma: we will do, and we will hear. Doing comes before hearing. Some teachers say that's why the learning took root.
A deed is physical. A carried box, a held door, a hand on a shoulder. You learn the weight of something by lifting it, not by reading about lifting.
Fourth, this isn't against learning. Avot is a book of sayings.
Wisdom matters; it just needs more deeds than it has words.

how: Jewish tradition pairs study with action: communities organize visits to the sick, meals for families in mourning, and giving, alongside classes and prayer.

o: act before thinking, since thinking slows you down
finish all your chores before you begin to study
let what you do outrun what you know, so wisdom lasts

games.q: doing and knowing — tap the pairs.
p: we will do, and we will hear

s: Avot says wisdom endures when deeds exceed it
at Sinai, the people said they'd understand first, then act
they said, all that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient: doing first.
deeds first means learning doesn't matter
wisdom matters; it just needs more deeds than words to last.

games.q: a new volunteer at a food bank wants to read everything about hunger before she helps. what does Avot 3:9 suggest?
o: start helping now, and let the learning grow alongside.
read everything first, since wisdom has to come first.
skip the reading entirely; knowing never helps doing.
games.why: Chanina ben Dosa doesn't drop wisdom. he says it lasts when deeds outrun it.

practice: Do one small thing with your hands right now, slowly: fold a towel, straighten a shelf, wash one cup. Feel the weight, the texture, the temperature of it. Let the hands lead, and let the mind stay quiet until the sit ends.

wordCard.voice: Deeds first: Chanina ben Dosa's rule that wisdom lasts when what you do outruns what you know.

carryVoice: Your line: deeds first. Na'aseh, then nishma: we will do, and we will hear. See you after the paint dries.
